pool.q: A circular economy is a change away from which model?
options: Resources are mined, made into products and then become waste
pool.explain: A circular economy keeps materials in use; material recovery plays an important role.
pool.evidence: It is a change to the model in which resources are mined, made into products, and then become waste.

pool.q: What are the major stages in a material's life cycle?
options: Raw material acquisition, materials manufacture, production, use/reuse/maintenance and waste management
pool.explain: Sustainable materials management looks at impacts across the whole life cycle.
pool.evidence: The major stages in a material’s lifecycle are raw material acquisition, materials manufacture, production, use/reuse/maintenance, and waste management.

pool.q: What does EPA mean by municipal solid waste (MSW), or trash?
options: Various items consumers throw away after they are used
pool.explain: Examples include bottles, boxes, food, grass clippings, furniture and appliances.
pool.evidence: EPA refers to trash, or MSW, as various items consumers throw away after they are used.

pool.q: What does the waste management hierarchy emphasise as key to sustainable materials management?
pool.explain: Options higher in the hierarchy keep materials in use and avoid disposal.
pool.evidence: The hierarchy places emphasis on reducing, reusing, and recycling as key to sustainable materials management.

pool.q: What does 'source reduction' mean?
options: Recycling waste where it is produced
Returning waste to the country it came from
Reducing waste before it enters the waste stream
pool.explain: The best waste is the waste that is never created.
pool.evidence: This includes the source reduction of wastes before they enter the waste stream

pool.q: Why did EPA's reported waste figures rise from 2017 to 2018?
options: Households threw away twice as many electronics
EPA started counting more wasted-food management pathways
pool.explain: A change in measurement, not just behaviour, can move statistics.
pool.evidence: inclusion of additional wasted food management pathways

pool.q: In the EU waste hierarchy, what is the preferred option, and what is the last resort?
options: Recycling is preferred; prevention is the last resort
Preventing waste is preferred; landfill is the last resort
Incineration is preferred; recycling is the last resort
Landfill is preferred; composting is the last resort
pool.explain: Order: prevention, preparing for re-use, recycling, other recovery, disposal.
pool.evidence: Preventing waste is the preferred option, and sending waste to landfill should be the last resort.

pool.q: Under the Waste Framework Directive, what is a by-product?
options: A substance from a production process whose main aim was not to produce it
A product returned by a customer
pool.explain: By-products that meet the conditions are not treated as waste.
pool.evidence: a substance or object resulting from a production process, the primary aim of which is not the production of that substance or object

pool.q: Under the revised directive, each Member State must set up an EPR scheme for which products?
pool.explain: Extended producer responsibility makes producers pay for managing their products as waste.
pool.evidence: This includes seeing each Member State set up its own EPR scheme for textile and footwear products.

pool.q: How much of the environmental damage caused when products become waste could be avoided by better decisions at the production stage?
pool.explain: Design decisions lock in most of a product's waste impact.
pool.evidence: Evidence suggests that 80% of the damage inflicted upon the environment when products become waste can be avoided if more thoughtful decisions are made at the production stage

pool.q: What does England's resources and waste strategy aim to eliminate by 2050?
pool.explain: Avoidable plastic waste is targeted over the lifetime of the 25 Year Environment Plan.
pool.evidence: eliminating avoidable waste of all kinds by 2050

pool.q: In a more circular economy, how long are resources kept in use?
options: Until they go out of fashion
As long as possible, to extract maximum value
pool.explain: Products and materials are then recovered and regenerated whenever possible.
pool.evidence: A more circular economy will see us keeping resources in use as long as possible, so we extract maximum value from them.

pool.q: Besides reducing and managing waste safely, what does the strategy promise to tackle?
pool.explain: Illegal dumping and waste fraud damage the environment and undercut legitimate operators.
pool.evidence: by reducing and managing waste safely and carefully, and by tackling waste crime

pool.q: What does the strategy plan to double?
pool.explain: Getting more value from each unit of material is at the heart of a circular economy.
pool.evidence: doubling resource productivity

pool.q: What is recycling?
options: Collecting and processing materials that would otherwise be thrown away and turning them into new products
pool.explain: Collection, processing and manufacturing into new products repeat as a loop.
pool.evidence: Recycling is the process of collecting and processing materials that would otherwise be thrown away as trash and turning them into new products.

pool.q: How many steps make up the recycling process represented by the chasing-arrows symbol?
options: Three, repeated in a continuous loop
pool.explain: Collection and processing, manufacturing, and buying recycled products form the loop.
pool.evidence: The recycling process is made up of three steps that are repeated over and over again.

pool.q: How does applying compost to land help the climate?
options: Carbon is stored in the soil instead of being released into the atmosphere
It cools the air above fields
It reflects sunlight back into space
pool.explain: Compost also builds soil health and supplies nutrients to plants.
pool.evidence: When we apply compost to the land, carbon is stored in the soil instead of being released into the atmosphere.

pool.q: What is composting?
options: Managed, aerobic decomposition of organic materials by microorganisms
Digesting waste in sealed tanks without oxygen
pool.explain: Composting needs oxygen; anaerobic digestion is a different process.
pool.evidence: Composting is the managed, aerobic (oxygen-required) biological decomposition of organic materials by microorganisms.

pool.q: Which materials count as organic for composting?
options: Grass clippings, leaves, yard trimmings and food scraps
pool.explain: Organic means carbon-based material that microorganisms can break down.
pool.evidence: Organic (carbon-based) materials include grass clippings, leaves, yard and tree trimmings, and food scraps.

pool.q: What is finished compost used for?
options: Building soil health and providing nutrients to plants
pool.explain: Compost is a biologically stable soil amendment.
pool.evidence: a biologically stable soil amendment that can be used to build soil health and provide nutrients to plants

pool.q: In home composting, what are 'browns'?
pool.explain: A good compost pile balances browns, greens and water.
pool.evidence: Carbon-rich materials (“browns”)

pool.q: Why do waste producers play a key role under the waste duty of care?
options: They set the price of disposal
They are in the best position to identify the nature and characteristics of the waste
pool.explain: An accurate description travels with the waste so it can be handled safely.
pool.evidence: Waste producers play a key role under the duty of care requirements as they are in the best position to identify the nature and characteristics of the waste.

pool.q: What is a householder's waste duty of care limited to?
options: Taking all reasonable measures to ensure their waste is only transferred to an authorised person
Keeping waste at home for a year
pool.explain: Using an unlicensed 'man with a van' can make householders liable.
pool.evidence: limited to taking all reasonable measures available to them to ensure their waste is only transferred to an authorised person.

pool.q: Before transferring waste to another person, what must a waste holder ensure?
options: That the person pays for it
That the waste is recycled abroad
That the person has the correct authorisation
That the waste is mixed with other waste
pool.explain: Transfers must go to registered carriers or permitted sites.
pool.evidence: Ensure that any person you transfer the waste to has the correct authorisation

pool.q: What must you provide when you transfer waste to another person?
options: An accurate description of the waste
pool.explain: The description lets the next holder manage the waste safely and legally.
pool.evidence: Provide an accurate description of the waste when it is transferred to another person

pool.q: What do environmental permits set out?
options: Specific conditions on how a waste operation must be carried out
pool.explain: Operators must follow the conditions in their permit.
pool.evidence: Environmental permits set out specific conditions on how a waste operation must be carried out.

pool.q: How is waste from a property used mainly for commercial business classed?
options: As commercial waste, subject to the duty of care
As hazardous waste in every case
pool.explain: Businesses run from homes still follow the commercial duty of care for that waste.
pool.evidence: Waste that comes from a property or part of a property that is mainly used for commercial business is regarded as commercial waste

pool.q: A landlord clears out student housing after the tenants leave. Is that household waste?
options: No — clearance waste from vacated premises is not household waste
pool.explain: The landlord therefore has the duty of care for it.
pool.evidence: Waste resulting from the clearance of premises after they have been vacated, such as a landlord or letting agent clearing student housing, is also not considered to be household waste.

pool.q: A builder produces waste while working on someone's home. Who is responsible for it?
options: The builder, who must meet their own duty of care and include disposal in their price
Nobody, because it is construction waste
pool.explain: Waste produced by a trader's work is the trader's waste.
pool.evidence: They must comply with their own duty of care obligations in relation to that waste, and the cost of its disposal should be included in what they charge for the work.

pool.q: What does end-of-life management for solar PV refer to?
options: What happens when panels and other system parts are retired
pool.explain: It covers panels and other components such as racking and inverters.
pool.evidence: End-of-life management for photovoltaics (PV) refers to the processes that occur when solar panels and other components of a PV system (racking, inverters, etc.) are retired from operation.

pool.q: How has the average operational lifespan of a solar panel changed?
options: From about 20 years in 2007 to 25–35 years in 2025
It has stayed at about 5 years
pool.explain: Longer lifespans delay when panels enter the waste stream.
pool.evidence: the average operational lifespan of a solar panel has increased from around 20 years in 2007 to 25-35 years in 2025

pool.q: What is 'repowering'?
options: Restarting panels after a power cut
Melting old panels into new ones
Upgrading solar panels early to benefit from better technology
pool.explain: Some owners replace panels before the warranty expires.
pool.evidence: may choose to upgrade their solar panels before the warranty period expires or to take advantage of technological improvements

pool.q: In the US, how does the cost of recycling solar panels compare with landfilling them?
pool.explain: Innovation aims to recover more materials at higher purity and lower cost.
pool.evidence: the total cost of recycling is still generally greater than the cost of disposing them in a landfill

pool.q: Which factors are expected to speed up solar panels reaching end of life?
pool.explain: More data is still needed on when, why and how many panels retire.
pool.evidence: weather damage and installation errors are expected to accelerate end-of-life issues

pool.q: According to the IEA, roughly what share of solar energy systems has been installed since 2019?
pool.explain: Most systems are young, so large waste volumes are still decades away.
pool.evidence: approximately 70% of solar energy systems have been installed since 2019

pool.q: How does projected US solar panel waste by 2030 compare with total US solid waste?
options: It is larger than all other waste combined
It is small next to about 200 million tons of solid waste a year
pool.explain: Projected PV waste is 0.17–1 million tons by 2030, but it will grow over the following decades.
pool.evidence: the Environmental Protection Agency estimates that there are 200 million tons of solid waste
